title: Who Gets to Shape AI? Why Girls Must Be in the Room
description:

title: From Tissue to Treatment
description:
Artificial intelligence is transforming drug discovery and clinical medicine - but AI is only as powerful as the data underlying it. The next frontier is not bigger datasets: it is spatially resolved datasets. Spatial multi-omics technologies can now simultaneously capture gene expression, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and protein abundance with precise X-Y tissue coordinates, creating a new class of tissue-level foundation models that transcend models based on bulk and single-cell data.

This panel brings together five leading scientists and technologists from Yale, Columbia, IAS Princeton, and KAUST to explore a pivotal question: How will spatial multi-omics reshape AI models for disease treatment across diverse ancestral backgrounds, and accelerate drug discovery from target identification to clinical validation?

title: Fighting deepfake in Age and Identity Verification
description:
Age and Identity verification is full of deepfakes. It is getting harder and harder to distinguish honest actors from fraudsters. 

The solution isn't that we use better AI tools to detect deepfakes - that is playing a losing battle. Rather we should be using authoritative sources and cryptography to verify user's identity. 

That is what Reclaim Protocol does (https://reclaimprotocol.org) - an open source verification system that uses zero knowledge proofs to verify users' identity. 

Come learn more, and discuss with others solving the same problem. Each participant will be hand picked, to maintain high density of like minded people. 

Looking forward to seeing you!

Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how humans interact with technology, and voice agents are emerging as one of the most powerful interfaces for AI applications. This workshop introduces developers to the foundations of agentic voice systems and shows how to build intelligent voice agents capable of interacting with users in real time.

Sponsored by Cloudonix, this hands-on demonstration workshop explores how developers can combine modern AI models with real-time voice infrastructure to create practical applications such as AI receptionists, automated service agents, and conversational assistants.

During the session, participants will learn how to use Dograh, an open-source framework for building agentic voice systems, together with the programmable voice infrastructure provided by Cloudonix.

What You’ll Learn
Participants will be introduced to the core components of an AI voice agent, including:
• How agentic AI systems interact with voice interfaces
 • The architecture of modern AI voice bots
 • Connecting AI models to real-time voice communication
 • Building a functional voice agent using open tools
 • Rapid prototyping techniques for voice-based applications

The workshop will include live demonstrations showing how a developer can go from concept to a working voice agent using open-source tools and cloud communications APIs.

Who Should Attend
This workshop is designed for:
• University students studying computer science or AI
 • Recent graduates interested in AI startups

 • Entrepreneurs interested in voice-enabled applications

title: Generative Computing Masterclass: Building Predictable, Auditable AI with Mellea.
description:
Speaker: Paul Schweigert, AI Foundations Engineer, IBM Research

In this masterclass, we’ll introduce Mellea, an
open‑source framework that treats large language models,
not as chat partners, but as programmable components
inside real applications. You’ll see how AI behavior can be
broken into clear, composable steps using the Instruct–
Validate–Repair pattern, with structured outputs and
grounded retrieval built in. The payoff: predictable,
auditable, and reproducible AI. Combined with smaller
open‑weight models like IBM’s Granite models, developers
are seeing performant, trustworthy results at a fraction of
the cost. We’ll close the session with a real‑world case
study that turns a stack of construction PDFs into a fully
cited cost estimate and report.

title: Causal Foresight with Anthos: Navigate Uncertainty with Better Decision-Making.
description:
​Leaders are regularly asked to make high-stakes decisions: where to invest, which interventions to prioritize, and how to allocate limited resources for the greatest impact. And these decisions only grow harder as systems become more deeply intertwined, consequences less predictable, and the stakes higher. Yet the tools we rely on weren't built for this. Large language models and conventional ML share a critical blind spot: they can't predict how a system will respond to an intervention it has never encountered before. To navigate today's complexity, we need tools that can reason beyond historical precedent and anticipate the downstream effects of the choices we make.

Anthos is a simulation platform that lets investors, philanthropies, and policymakers stress-test decisions before they commit capital or sign policy. It ingests the relevant literature, then applies neuro-symbolic causal inference to model the second- and third-order consequences spreadsheets and standard forecasting tend to miss. Non-technical users can run "what-if" scenarios through conversational AI and quickly see whether an investment thesis or policy proposal holds up under pressure.

Be among the first to experience Anthos. In this intimate, hands-on workshop, founders Devin Young (CEO) and DJ Passey (CTO) — joined by advisor C. Robin Castelli, MSc (former Global Head of Climate Modeling Analytics at Citi) and World Bank design partner Jasmin Sadegh — will run live model demonstrations. Then you'll have the chance to build your own causal models in Anthos, guided by our AI agents.

title: Design Thinking Meets AI: Book Talk & Live Build
description:
AI can write the code now, but who's designing what it builds? Louise Macfadyen, author of the newly released O'Reilly book, Designing AI Interfaces, joins Bethany Crystal for a conversation that starts with a deceptively simple question: What does it mean to design AI-native systems and interfaces?

​Together they'll explore the philosophy and surprises of designing AI systems, poking at questions like: Who counts as a designer now? What does good taste looks like in a prompt-driven world? What happens when the coding is the easy part? Then they'll put it to the test.

Bethany and Louise will take a design concept from the book and build it live, in real time (using AI), showing what it looks like when design thinking drives the engineering, not the other way around. They'll close with a reflection on what worked, what surprised them, and what it means for anyone building with AI today.

​Key Takeaways:

- ​Understand the core principles of AI interface design from the author who literally wrote the book on it

- ​Watch design thinking applied live, from concept to working prototype in real time

​- Rethink your own role: You don't need to be a "designer" to start designing better AI experiences

​Target Audience:

- ​Product managers, designers, and builders working on AI-powered products who want a sharper design lens

- ​Founders and operators using AI tools daily who want to move from "it works" to "it works well" and understand why the difference matters

- ​Copies of the book, Designing AI Interfaces, will be available for purchase.

​—

title: What Quantum Actually Means for Computing
description:
For years, quantum computing was seen as a breakthrough perpetually just out of reach. That perception is beginning to shift. Scientists are now combining quantum and classical systems to address problems that become prohibitively complex at scale, especially in molecular modeling, chemistry, materials science, and energy. This session will explore what has enabled recent progress, what quantum computing can deliver today, the importance of building a quantum workforce for today and for the future, and how the gap between long‑term promise and practical impact is starting to narrow.

title: How to Write a Book on AI in Enterprise SDLC While Patterns Keep Changing
description:
New model drops. New framework. New "this changes everything" thread. By the time you've integrated one tool, three more have made it obsolete.

So we asked ourselves a different question: what doesn't change? Across enterprise teams, across codebases, across the hype cycles. Which engineering practices actually hold up when the underlying models rotate every quarter?

Artur Skowroński and Tomasz Lelek spent a year shipping AI-assisted code across enterprise clients, watching what broke and what survived, then committed the patterns to print in Vibe Engineering: Best practices, mistakes, and tradeoffs, co-published with Manning Publications.

Join Artur and Tomasz for a discussion panel and community mixer, and learn about:
- Where AI earns its place in the delivery cycle, and where it creates new debt 
- Vibe coding beyond the individual contributor: what changes at team and org scale
- Keeping quality and trust intact when half your code has a co-author 
- Staying fast without losing control of what ships

And if you are interested in writing a book yourself, Artur and Tomasz will also talk about:
- Picking the right topic, so that the trend is still relevant when the book is out
- Getting past the writer’s block
- What reputable publishers like Manning are actually looking for right now

After the panel, you are invited over for drinks, networking, and the kind of conversations that don't happen in Slack.

Bonus: We'll be giving away 30 demo copies of Vibe Engineering: Best practices, mistakes, and tradeoffs. Grab one and get it signed by Artur and Tomasz in person.

title: Building Safe Agents for Business
description:
AI agents are moving from demos to production. They execute payments, write code, access sensitive data, and ship decisions to clients without a human in the loop. 

The safety infrastructure has not kept up, and this workshop is focused on fixing that.

Today's guardrails are assertions, not proofs. They only work most of the time, fail silently in the cases that matter, and can be hijacked by a single line of injected text. Every public agent incident ends with the same question: how do you prove the agent followed the rule?

We'll learn how missing layer is cryptographic guarantees, not better prompts or more filters: mathematical proof that an agent action complies with your policy before it runs.  

This workshop teaches you how to easily build formal verification of agent policy before each action; defenses that survive prompt injection; and portable receipts your security team, counterparty and your auditor can easily verify. 

Hands-on and accessible to all - we hope to see you there!

title: The Internet of Building Things
description:
HardTech Forum hosted by MistyWest (www.mistywest.com) and presented by Intent (https://www.withintent.com/)

---

Since Kevin Ashton coined "Internet of Things" in 1999, the promise of real-time tracking has finally become practical, built on RFID, BLE, cellular telematics, and satellite connectivity. Devices now run 10 years on a single battery, and new systems are experimenting with Bluetooth signals detected directly by satellites.

After our April 9th Vancouver HardTech Forum on The Internet of Moving Things, MistyWest and Intent are bringing the conversation to NYC with The Internet of Building Things. Construction is one of the hardest environments to digitize—chaotic, temporary, and GPS-denied—but autonomous drones, LiDAR, and adapted fleet sensor stacks are changing that fast. This HardTech Forum asks: now that we can see the physical world with unprecedented resolution, where does the real value get created, in the hardware, the data, or the platforms that turn sensor feeds into decisions?

---
SPEAKERS

Ben Williams - COO at Exyn Technologies (www.exyn.com/)

Ben is the COO/CPO of Exyn Technologies, pioneering GPS-denied autonomy in multi-modal robots. Previously, he co-founded and led Reelio (acquired by Fullscreen Media/AT&T), helped commercialize deep tech at Lockheed Martin, and earned his MBA from Wharton — where he was later named to their 40 Under 40. A former US Naval Officer and recovering engineer, he also mentors early-stage startups and serves on various boards, all while keeping his two young sons out of the snack cabinet.

Join Adobe for a special gathering that goes beyond the AI conversation to explore what meaningful transparency looks like across the creative ecosystem: who made something, how it was made, and why that matters, whether you're an illustrator, a builder, or a startup founder scaling to enterprise. 

Content Credentials is the global standard for digital provenance, securely attaching verifiable information to content, including photos, videos, audio, and generative AI, proving the origins of media and how it was created, composited, and edited. title: Fin x Clay: Scaling CX in the AI Era
description:
When adopting customer-facing AI, companies often start with service. But now, the most forward-thinking teams are taking a more holistic approach. They're not just using an AI Agent for service – they're collapsing the walls between support, success, and sales, to build a more a connected customer experience.

For Clay, the transformation is already underway. They've embedded GTM engineering into Ops teams to drive support efficiency at scale. Support Engineering is placed at the intersection of CX teams to reduce volume by fixing issues and building internal tools. Support and Success are becoming more collaborative— moving from focusing volume management to building durable customer relationships.

Fin is building toward the same future — a single Customer Agent that delivers a seamless customer experience — from sales to service to success.

Join Declan Ivory, VP of Customer Support at Fin / Intercom, and George Dilthey, Head of Support at Clay, for an honest conversation about what scaling CX with AI actually looks like in practice — the org changes, the use cases you haven't tried yet, and where this is all heading.

title: LOCK UP AI?
description:
In partnership with the Healthcare Club of NY and Caseflow AI (usecaseflow.ai) for NY TECH WEEK.

New York is about to decide something the rest of the country will be watching: whether chatbot companies should be on the hook when their AI gives medical, legal, or mental health advice that causes harm.

Senate Bill S7263, sponsored by State Senator Kristen Gonzalez, would make chatbot operators civilly liable when their AI provides "substantive" advice in domains covered by professional licensing law. That's 14+ licensed professions plus the practice of law. Disclaimers don't save you. A "you're talking to a bot" notice doesn't save you. And the private right of action means anyone harmed can sue.

Supporters say it's common sense: if a human pretending to be a doctor can be prosecuted, a chatbot that hallucinates a medical license shouldn't get a free pass. Critics say the bill is vague about what counts as "substantive" advice, puts nonprofit and government chatbots in the same legal crosshairs as OpenAI, and ends up taxing the people who most need low-cost information (tenants, patients, small business owners) on behalf of licensed incumbents who don't love the competition.
Both sides have a point. That's why we're putting them in a room.

Against S7263:
Sateesh Nori: attorney, legal tech founder (LawDroid), and one of the more thoughtful voices arguing that restricting AI legal guidance hurts the people the legal system already fails.

For S7263:
Dr. Cecilia Dones: data and analytics practitioner-academic, founder of 3 Standard Deviations, and a faculty member at Columbia's School of Professional Studies. Her work sits at the intersection of AI, data, and trust: translating what these systems actually do for organizations, consumers, and the people who get caught in between.

title: Build Your Team for the Agentic Era
description:
Build your team for the AI Era: A working session for founders and operators

Not a panel. Not a presentation. A hands-on session where you leave with something real.

Most teams are letting people go, handing work to agents, and then realizing no one knows how to manage, debug, or course-correct when things break. The org chart isn't just a people problem anymore and most teams have no framework for thinking about it.

What we'll do:

Part 1: Design Getting everyone on the same page, literally. We'll start with a shared vocabulary (what is an AI agent vs. AI, what is an AI Orchestrator, where do agents sit in a reporting structure) and then work through how to reimagine an org chart with both human and agent roles mapped explicitly. Where does discretion live? Where does transactional work get handed off? Who owns the system when it breaks?

Part 2: Implementation Once the design is clear, the harder question: how do you actually build toward it? This is where workflow architecture, change management, and the culture of how humans and agents operate together come into focus.

What you'll walk away with:

1) A reimagined version of your org structure and new roles identified, handoffs mapped. 
2) A "Before & After" org chart visualization showing where agents plug in and where humans move up to Orchestrator. 
3) An AI usage diagnostic: where you are vs. where you could be

***Bring your laptop to be able to participate in the session.

Why Britt & Mina: Britt has spent four years deploying fractional operators onto early and growth-stage teams, a model that's essentially a preview of where all teams are heading. Mina brings the AI implementation layer, including a sharp framework for thinking about agents the way we once thought about org hierarchy. Together: here's how to design it, and here's how to build it.

title: Humans, Robots & The Factory Floor
description:
As robotics and automation accelerate across industries, most conversations remain abstract and focused on technology capabilities rather than real world deployment. 

Robotics adoption in U.S. manufacturing is accelerating. Nearly 400,000 industrial robots are now operating in U.S. factories, with tens of thousands added each year. At the same time, manufacturing continues to face a labor gap measured in the hundreds of thousands of open roles, with millions more projected this decade. But adoption is not the same as success. Most automation challenges do not fail at the level of technology. They fail on the factory floor, where people, process, training, safety, and operating constraints
determine whether systems work or stall.

Humans + Robots & The Factory Floor brings together operators, robotics companies, and systems leaders to explore what happens when automation meets the real world of production.

This session moves to examine the lived experience of integrating robotics into active manufacturing environments.

Why This Matters Now
Robotics adoption is increasing, but deployment challenges remain widespread. Many automation efforts fail not because of the technology itself, but because of misalignment with human systems.

Workforce, training, and operational realities are too often excluded from innovation conversations.

There is a growing need to connect startups, manufacturers, and workforce leaders in a shared dialogue.

This event addresses a critical gap by focusing on the intersection of technology an

New York Robotics (NYR) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing the robotics and embodied AI industry across the regional, national, and global landscape — becoming a driving force for innovation, investment, and industry growth, positioning New York as a premier global hub for robotics

Most deep tech and AI founders treat IP as paperwork — something to get to before the next round, handled by outside counsel, forgotten until diligence. Meanwhile, the companies that treat their patent portfolio as a financial instrument are raising at multiples their competitors can't touch.
What actually changed: AI has rewritten what's patentable, what should stay a trade secret, and how investors diligence a moat. Post-Thaler, post-2024 USPTO guidance on AI-assisted inventions, the rules your lawyer learned in 2019 aren't the rules anymore. The founders who understand this are repricing their companies. title: Fireside chat: The Trust Transfer
description:
What does it actually take to get people to trust something new with the things they care about? The founders on this panel have answered that question twice, ten years apart.

They built Venmo, Stripe, and the consumer fintech rails that now feel obvious. Getting people to send money through an app was a fight. Now they're in a different one: convincing engineers to share how they prompt, and convincing everyone else to trust a cloud computer with their files, their work, and their ideas.

Same trust barrier. Different decade. Same people figuring it out.

We're getting into the pattern match between early consumer fintech and where AI is right now (what's the same, what's actually new), the shift from mobile-first to AI-first and what that means for how you build, hire, and sell, when to take an exit vs. keep building, and how tribal knowledge inside a team turns from advantage into bottleneck. 

We'll close rapid-fire: best advice you ignored, advice you're ignoring right now.

Bring questions. Leave with quotes.

title: Agents in Production: The Memory Problem
description:
Agent memory is a mess. 

Most teams are stitching together a vector store, a graph database, and some middleware - three systems to manage, three potential failure points, and no guarantees any of it stays consistent. It works until it doesn't.

This meetup is about solving it properly. Not a quick fix, not another abstraction layer - memory that's transactional, structured, and built into the database itself. We'll show what that looks like in practice with Spectron, SurrealDB's brand new agent memory system.

We'll be joined by engineering teams from Pydantic and Tavily - covering how to structure and validate the data your agents work with, and how to handle retrieval at runtime without losing the plot mid-task.

Hard questions welcome. Drinks on us.

title: Is Software the New Fast Fashion? Happy Hour Roundtables at #NYTechWeek
description:
Fashion's been doing this for 20 years. Tech, welcome to the chat.

This is the direction tech is headed: AI writes the code, nobody maintains it, everyone rebuilds from scratch every six months. Custom tools nobody documented. Codebases that sprawl like a Shein cart. 
(Scott's take: https://worksonmymachine.ai/p/entering-technical-debts-zirp-era)

This is what fashion has been doing for twenty years: make it cheap, make it fast, make it disposable, make it again. A closet full of things you don't remember buying and a trillion dollars in returns and waste. (Nancy's take: https://repairera.substack.com/p/earth-month-is-a-trap)

The question is whether tech learns from fashion's mistake, or repeats it at a new scale.

This Tech Week, we're hosting a happy hour of guided roundtables across tech, fashion, ops, & sustainability. 

Expert hosts leading conversations on different angles of the theme. Everyone has a chance to bring their perspective. Topics like what fast fashion does right, what tech can learn from fashion (and vice versa), infrastructure nobody sees, and what "buy it for life" means in 2026.

Expect cross-industry collaboration, a few drinks, a few laughs, and maybe some insight on how to move forward.

Tech bros, fashion girlies, investors looking for the moat, and sustainability folks who saw this coming. 
All are welcome. 

Co-hosted by 
Nancy Rhodes (Alternew, The Repair Era) and 
Scott Werner (Artificial Ruby, Sublayer).

By registering, you'll be subscribed to Works on My Machine and The Repair Era. Consider it homework for the roundtable.

description:
This event is a fireside chat + mixer for a curated room of founders, researchers, physicians, and angel investors in the neurotech space to gather to exchange ideas, forge meaningful relationships, and discuss the state of the evolving neurotech field. By bridging the gap between biological intelligence, AI, and governance systems, we aim to catalyze the breakthroughs that will define the next decade of cognitive enhancement and computational neuroscience.  

This event will be part of a series of NeuroNYC's newest NeuroAI initiative. Large scale AI models are being built for the brain, neural interfaces are moving from lab to clinic, and AI architectures are increasingly drawing inspiration from neuroscience. As these technologies advance, so do the ethical and governance questions they raise: who owns neural data, and what guardrails should guide AI systems modeled on or decoding the brain? These challenges demand expertise that no single discipline can provide alone. New York City sits at a unique crossroads of neuroscience, AI, medicine, engineering, ethics, and policy talent, and that's what NeuroAI aims to bridge.

Bringing together perspectives from brand, technology, and commerce infrastructure, this conversation will focus on how AI agents can empower merchants and strengthen the direct connection between brands and their customers, rather than replacing it with big tech models designed only to operate within their own infrastructure.

Speaker bios:
Dori Yona
Dori started SimpleClosure after facing a tough moment in his own business when he needed help closing down a company but couldn't find good advice anywhere. After running an app called Earny that millions of people used, he knew there had to be a better way to help business owners close their companies. His new company, SimpleClosure, now helps hundreds of other business owners shut down their companies faster and cheaper than traditional methods. Based in Santa Monica with his family, Dori works to show that closing a business doesn't have to be scary or hard, and that learning from tough experiences can lead to helping others.

Jesse Carey
Jesse Carey leads growth for Stripe Atlas, Stripe’s startup incorporation platform. He previously served as Business Operations Lead at Headway, a mental health startup, where he launched the company’s government business. Prior, he was a Strategy & Planning Manager at Uber Eats and a management consultant focused on payments. He holds an MBA from Harvard Business School after attending Sydney Law School, having moved to the US from Australia in 2017.

Sam Garcia
Sam Garcia is a Partner with the Amplo platform of Collective Global. Sam focuses on the Seed/Series A practice at Amplo and serves on the boards of Lightyear, Flume, Kredi, Tradespace, Wizehire, Steno, Axion Ray, Doxel, and previously served on the board of Legalpad until they were acquired by Deel. Walk in with an idea. Walk out with a live, deployed MVP — and a shot at $25,000 in Azure credits.

This is a hands-on, full-day hackathon for founders, PMs, and builders who want to ship real software using GitHub Copilot and agentic AI workflows — no deep engineering background required. 

We'll start with a masterclass from Miguel Martinez, Principal AI Solutions Engineer at Microsoft, covering the GitHub Copilot fundamentals, prompt patterns, and agentic workflows that turn ideas into working code. 
Then you'll team up (teams of 3–4) and spend the afternoon in a focused build sprint, with Microsoft mentors roaming the room to unblock you.
By 4pm, you'll demo a working product to our judging panel. One team walks away with $25,000 in Azure credits from Microsoft for Startups.

Who should come: Non-technical founders and PMs who want to build the MVP they've been putting off. Engineers who want to ship fast and meet founders. Anyone curious about what's actually possible with AI-assisted coding in 2026.

In this interactive lab, you'll get a crash course in vibe coding fundamentals, then open your laptop and start building - with real-time feedback from those who do this every day. We'll close with live demos where volunteers share what they built and get feedback from the room.

title: Bring Your Product. We'll Break It.
description:
Bring Your Product. We'll Break It.

Live adversarial testing for 10 AI-native founders. 60 minutes. Real vulnerabilities. Coffee provided.

Your product ships fast. Your attackers move faster.

Most early-stage companies think security is something to solve later, after scale, after growth, after fundraising. But modern products are being probed from day one by bots, automated scripts, AI-assisted attackers, and increasingly sophisticated threat actors.

In this 60-minute live session, we’ll simulate how real attackers evaluate a product and show you where your system breaks before the internet does.

Using controlled offensive security methods, the Tequity Security Ops team will:

— Map your exposed attack surface across product, infrastructure, workflows, and user behavior
— Demonstrate how seemingly small vulnerabilities compound into major security risks
— Identify trust and security gaps across authentication, permissions, APIs, AI systems, internal tooling, and operational workflows
— Show how attackers think, move, escalate access, and exploit assumptions inside modern products
— Help you understand what security maturity actually looks like for a zero-to-one company

This is not a theoretical webinar. It is a live working session.

Bring your product, staging environment, prototype, or architecture. We’ll walk through real-world attack scenarios and show you where your company is most vulnerable today.

You’ll leave with:

* A high-level risk assessment of your current product ecosystem
* A practical understanding of your most critical vulnerabilities
* A security prioritization framework for your current stage
* Recommendations on what to fix immediately vs later
* A clearer picture of what modern Security Ops should look like inside a growing startup

Who this is for:
— Founders building AI-native or SaaS products
— Engineering teams moving quickly without dedicated security leadership
— Startups handling sensitive user, healthcare, fintech, or enterprise

title: Wear Your Coach: A Live Wearable Movement Demo
description:
Name: Wear Your Coach: A Live Wearable Movement Demo
description:
A live wearable tech demo + networking event at Tech Week 2026
Ever finish a workout, a yoga flow, or a stretch routine and wonder if you actually did it right? Most of us have no idea when our bodies are compensating, tilting, or drifting off course. LumbarGuide makes the invisible visible — and tonight, you get to feel it yourself.
This hands-on demo event puts a working wearable biofeedback system directly on attendees. No slides. No theory. Just real-time haptic feedback the moment your body moves wrong.
The evening features:
🏋️ Plank Station — "How Long Can You Actually Hold It Right?" Think you know how to plank? Strap on the device and find out. The wearable detects the moment your lower back starts to sag, tracks your hold time, and buzzes when the clock runs out. No more guessing. No more cheating yourself.
🧍 Scoliosis Simulation — "Now Imagine Doing This Alone, Every Day" Watch a short clinical rehab video — as many times as you want, just like a real patient would after a clinic visit. Then try to replicate the movement from memory. The sensor will tell you if your correction went the right direction, if your pelvis compensated, and whether you held it correctly. Most people are humbled. All people get it.
🤝 Networking — Connect with founders, healthtech investors, engineers, and wellness enthusiasts in a casual, participatory setting.

Hear from the founder behind LumbarGuide — originally built to help adolescents with lumbar scoliosis practice rehabilitation exercises accurately at home using dual IMU sensors, it revealed something much more universal: most of us move through life with zero feedback on whether we're doing it right when the professionals aren’t around.
Whether you're into wearables, healthtech, fitness, or just curious what it feels like when a device knows your body better than you do — you'll leave this event moving differently.
No medical background needed. Just brin

description:
You can go from idea to demo software in seconds: you can describe a product, generate code, spin up agents, automate tasks, and create the illusion of instant execution; but your workflow fragments as soon as you pass demo and try to go live.

You're suddenly managing coding agents, orchestration layers, terminals, cloud consoles, API keys, Git workflows, deployment scripts, security questions, and broken handoffs between tools that were never designed to operate as one system.

Come to hear about bridging the gap between AI-generated software and production-ready execution.

We'll explore why the next major opportunity in developer tooling is not just another coding agent, model wrapper, or chat-based IDE forked from VS Code.

Ask → Explore → Edit → Validate → Install → Push → Deploy

We'll cover:

* Why AI has compressed idea-to-code, but not idea-to-production
* Why the current developer stack is becoming more powerful but more fragmented
* Why agents need a control layer, not just more autonomy
* How to unify coding, validation, Git, install, deployment, and local/cloud AI workflows
* Why native performance, privacy, and workflow completion matter in the next IDE category

The session will close with a brief introduction to Aurelian Labs, the NYC based venture studio and first backer behind LingCode: a native AI development environment; and its broader thesis on building infrastructure companies for the AI-native economy.

This is for you if you're a founder, developer, investor, engineer, operator, or builder trying to understand what comes after AI code gen or who wants to stop using 50+ tools to make one software.

title: Stop Making AI Guess: When Your Codebase Becomes the Spec
description:
If AI should read codebase structure rather than guess at it, why doesn't it?

AI coding tools work by reading source files and inferring architecture. The result is "almost-usable" code that requires manual refactoring. 

The deeper problem isn't the tools — it's that most frameworks weren't designed to be read structurally.  There's no layer for AI to reason against, so the tools are stuck guessing.

SpyneJS is an open-source framework designed for AI-assisted development.  It exposes a structural codemap that gives agents a deterministic understanding of application structure.

Refined over six years in enterprise environments, the framework is designed so generated code respects architectural boundaries from the first prompt.

Join us for a live demo of frontend codegen that holds up under peer review.  We'll show how agents interact with SpyneJS to produce structurally sound features, then discuss what becomes possible when the codebase itself functions as a working specification.

For developers, founders, and anyone evaluating where serious frontend development goes next.

title: AI Agents in the Wild: A Candid Conversation on Trust and Accountability
description:
We’re deploying AI agents faster than we can verify them. Ezio is changing that narrative.

As AI agents take on increasingly consequential roles, the question of trust has never been more urgent. What does it actually mean to trust AI agents and how do you build responsible infrastructure? Trust in AI agents is still largely improvised - based on intuition, brand, or retrospective debugging - rather than something measurable, inspectable, and enforced at the system level.

We’re convening the best group of leading VCs, founders, academics, and product leaders in New York to explore a core question: what does it truly mean to trust AI systems - and what would it take to build a reliable trust layer around them? Through a focused panel and small-group roundtables, we’ll move beyond surface-level conversations and examine questions like:

-How should we evaluate agents that plan, reason, and take multi-step actions?
-What does reliability mean in systems that evolve across tool use, memory, and environment?
-Where are the current blind spots in agent evaluation, monitoring, and control?
-What signals - technical or behavioral - could make agent trustworthiness observable in real time?

Grounded in lessons from high-stakes domains like finance and healthcare - where risk is modeled, audited, and continuously monitored - we’ll explore how similar principles might translate (or fail to translate) to modern AI systems. Topics will include hallucination and bias detection, evaluation blind spots, human-in-the-loop design, and emerging approaches to quantifying model reliability.

There is “responsible AI” as a principle. But this is a working session on something more concrete: how to move from intuition-based trust to system-level guarantees - and what needs to exist, technically and institutionally, for that shift to happen.

title: Women Shaping the Future of Fintech
description:
Women Shaping the Future of Fintech is a gathering by WomenX that brings together women working across finance, technology, startups, investing, and fintech.

As fintech continues to evolve, we believe women already play a critical role in shaping this space. We hope their voices can be heard, their experiences can be shared, and that they can build a community where they feel supported and connected.

At this event, we will invite women from companies such as Stripe, Goldman Sachs, PayPal, Apollo, Mastercard, and fintech startups. They will share how they work at the intersection of finance and technology, and how they see fintech evolving across payments, banking, investing, private markets, and AI-driven financial products.

After the talks, there will be a networking session where speakers and attendees can connect more freely and build meaningful relationships.

To keep the community thoughtful and relevant, attendance will be curated. We ask applicants to share materials such as a resume, portfolio, LinkedIn, personal website, or any platform that reflects their work or interests.

We hope this can be a space to meet, learn, and support one another.

title: The Future of Relocation: AI, Fintech & Logistics Converging
description:
Event Description

The global relocation and moving industry—worth over $100B annually—remains one of the most fragmented, opaque, and operationally inefficient markets today.

We’re bringing together a curated group of founders, operators, and investors to explore how AI, embedded finance, and marketplace infrastructure are transforming physical relocation into a scalable, data-driven category.

Hosted by MoveSwitcher, this private session will dive into the intersection of:

AI-powered logistics and dynamic pricing
Marketplace infrastructure for labor and fleet coordination
Embedded finance: payments, escrow, and insurance in relocation
Data as the foundation for next-generation mobility platforms

The evening will include a short, focused discussion followed by a live product demo of MoveSwitcher—an emerging platform designed to become the operating system for global relocation.

This is not a traditional networking event. Attendance is limited to ensure high-signal conversations and meaningful connections among participants building and backing the next generation of marketplaces and infrastructure companies.
